meta.title: Heart-rate variability: time and frequency domain
meta.tools: Pan–Tompkins R peaks (eelab.bio) on MIT-BIH record 100, time-domain HRV, Lomb–Scargle spectrum (SciPy)
meta.summary: Compute SDNN, RMSSD, pNN50 and LF/HF power from detected R peaks of a 30-minute real ECG, and check each metric against the same metric computed from the cardiologist's beat annotations.
meta.problem: HRV is widely used as a stress/fitness marker. How sensitive are the numbers to the beat detector that produces them?
meta.theory:
SDNN = std of NN intervals; RMSSD = √mean(ΔNN²) (short-term, vagal); LF 0.04–0.15 Hz and HF 0.15–0.4 Hz powers of the unevenly sampled RR series
(Lomb–Scargle avoids resampling). A timing error of σ_t per beat adds ≈ 2σ_t² to the successive-difference variance, so RMSSD is the most
detector-sensitive metric (e.g. a 3 ms jitter adds ~4 ms² to RMSSD²).
meta.method:
Record 100 (normal sinus rhythm with rare ectopics), full 30 min, 360 Hz. NN series = normal-to-normal intervals (ectopic beats and their neighbours
removed using the annotations for both series, so only detector timing differs). Metrics from detected vs annotated peaks.

rows.quantity: SDNN: detected peaks vs annotation reference
RMSSD: detected peaks vs annotation reference
